decision.detail: I cap the lens. The charge is dead, the little red light on the side just goes dark, and I don't reach for another battery because there isn't one. I slide the camera into the case, zip it, tuck the strap under my arm. I'm still standing in front of the screen where Alma talked to her girl in Pittsburgh. She's quiet now. I don't turn to her. I don't say goodnight. I don't say *that was good* or *she sounded like a kid* or any of the stuff. I just stand there a second, hands on the case, and then I walk out the door. The street's cold. February. I can see the ballroom from here, lights spilling out, and the station line is open, and Rita's got her recording up on the patch already, and I can feel the whole thing going on without me and that's fine. I don't go in. I don't deliver the reel. I walk to the hotel, sit in the lobby, put my boots on the side of the couch. The crew's there, finishing coffee, the ballroom footage on the little monitor. I don't look at it. I keep the reel in the case on my lap. I'll watch it in my room tonight or I won't. It's done. The Rialto won't be done by morning. The lights will be on again. I close my eyes.
decision.intention: Keep the reel. Don't hand it to the patch. Don't screen anything I don't have. Go home, sit in the lobby, let the evening pass over me, and let the party be the party. One take. It's in the case. That's the whole job.
decision.words: Nothing. Not to Alma. Not to the crew. Not to the street. Just the zip of the case and my boots on the lobby carpet and the muffled sound of the ballroom through the wall, and then quiet.
